subject: literature
passage: Bilal had always thought of the orchard outside Quetta as his uncle's place, somewhere to visit for a day at Eid and then forget. This summer, sent to help with the apricot harvest, he spent the first days counting the hours until his bus home. By the second week, though, he had learned which branches would bend without breaking and how to tell a ripe fruit by its softness under his thumb. On the last morning, when his uncle asked whether he would come back next year, Bilal was surprised to hear himself answer before the question was finished.
stem: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

choices.A: Bilal goes from wanting to leave the orchard to wanting to return to it.
choices.B: Bilal finds the apricot harvest more tiring than he had expected.
choices.C: Bilal agrees to return to the orchard only because his uncle insists.
choices.D: Bilal learns several useful skills during his second week in the orchard.

explanation.why: At first Bilal is "counting the hours until his bus home." By the end, he answers his uncle's invitation to return "before the question was finished," which shows eagerness. The text as a whole traces this change in his feelings about the orchard.
explanation.A: Correct. This captures the change from counting the hours until he can leave to eagerly agreeing to come back.
explanation.B: Incorrect. The text never says the work tires him.
explanation.C: Incorrect. Bilal answers before his uncle even finishes asking, so he is eager, not pressured.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The skills he learns are a step in his change, not the main point of the whole text.
